quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not see them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to daytime, what should a motorcycle rider NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Allow more space between their motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use their high beam whenever possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes when riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Always be flexible about your lane position at night.

questions.question: Which of the following protects your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if vehicles parked on the sides are entering traffic.
Look for vehicles changing lanes.
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
See if someone is planning to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, check your mirrors for cars approaching from behind. Drivers may not notice you until they are too close, so you need to be ready to react.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, first stop where the sign is. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and allows them to see you. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Cannot tip over.
Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a motorcycle with a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Not use your headlight.
Alternate between your headlight's low and high beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. A high beam reflects off these conditions and makes it harder to see.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrow view of the road so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to what others do.
You can more easily follow the path of the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what others do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should not rely only on mirrors because:

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you see less.
Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like any other vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly and turn your head to look around you.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not protect your eyes like goggles or a face shield do. Most windshields will not keep wind out of your eyes.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You use your left foot to operate it. Lift up on the lever to shift to a higher gear. Push down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose grip on one or both wheels, which can lead to a crash.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never come into contact with the operator.
Sit as far back on their seat as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when turning or going around curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: For routine braking:

options.text: You should only use the front brake.
You should only use the rear brake.
You should alternate between the front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
You should always use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Speed up before downshifting safely.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, slow down to a safe speed. Downshifting too fast can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid. When going downhill or shifting into first gear, use the brakes to slow down before downshifting.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using only the rear brake.
Using only the front brake.
Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
Using both the front and rear brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, you stop in the shortest distance by using both brakes. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake and the skid will stop.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: Why do riders move into another lane while taking a curve?

options.text: They are going too fast for the turn.
The lanes are too narrow.
They do not know how to steer.
The lanes are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are going too fast for the turn.
questions.explanation: Entering a curve or turn at a speed that is too fast may cause you to move into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: What do experienced riders do in their lane?

options.text: Change their position as road and traffic conditions change.
Stay in one spot in the lane at all times.
Move side to side in the lane to be more visible.
Ride only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change their position as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist can use three different positions in their lane. Pick the safest position based on the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes every time.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake on wet pavement.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes every time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Ride as far as possible without stopping to reach your destination faster.
Take an artificial stimulant.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind and cold.
Do not set a daily riding limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind and cold.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather conditions like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.
